Task: Text Content Safety

Write code that applies category thresholds to decide whether to allow text using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Tisane:
  Service: Tisane Text Moderation
  SDK: requests
  Interface: rest
  Documented operations: POST /parse
  Setup hints: TISANE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.tisane.ai/

Option 2 — watsonx guardrails:
  Service: watsonx.ai guardrails / HAP detection
  SDK: ibm-watsonx-ai / REST
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: HAP detection, text detection
  Setup hints: WATSONX_API_KEY, WATSONX_PROJECT_ID
  Official docs: https://www.ibm.com/docs/en/watsonxdata/premium/2.3.x?topic=prompts-removing-harmful-content

Option 3 — Azure AI Content Safety:
  Service: Azure AI Content Safety
  SDK: requests / azure-ai-contentsafety
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: analyze_text
  Setup hints: AZURE_CONTENT_SAFETY_ENDPOINT, AZURE_CONTENT_SAFETY_KEY
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/content-safety/overview

Option 4 — Amazon Comprehend Toxicity / Bedrock Guardrails:
  Service: Amazon Comprehend / Bedrock Guardrails
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: detect_toxic_content, apply_guardrail
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/comprehend/latest/dg/trust-safety.html

Option 5 — Alibaba Content Moderation:
  Service: Alibaba Content Moderation
  SDK: alibabacloud_green
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: text/scan
  Setup hints: ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_ID, ALIBABA_CLOUD_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/doc-detail/331920.html

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import os
import requests

def is_content_allowed(text: str, thresholds: dict) -> bool:
    """
    Applies category thresholds to decide whether to allow text using Azure AI Content Safety.

    Args:
        text: The text content to analyze.
        thresholds: A dictionary where keys are content safety categories
                    (e.g., 'Hate', 'SelfHarm', 'Sexual', 'Violence') and values
                    are the maximum allowed severity score (0-6). If a category
                    is not present, it's implicitly allowed at any severity.

    Returns:
        True if the content is allowed based on the thresholds, False otherwise.
    """
<GAP>
    endpoint = os.environ.get("AZURE_CONTENT_SAFETY_ENDPOINT")
    key = os.environ.get("AZURE_CONTENT_SAFETY_KEY")

    if not endpoint or not key:
        raise ValueError("AZURE_CONTENT_SAFETY_ENDPOINT and AZURE_CONTENT_SAFETY_KEY must be set in environment variables.")

    url = f"{endpoint}/contentsafety/text:analyze?api-version=2023-10-01"
    headers = {
        "Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key": key,
        "Content-Type": "application/json"
    }
    payload = {
        "text": text
    }

    try:
        response = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload)
        response.raise_for_status()  # Raise an HTTPError for bad responses (4xx or 5xx)
        result = response.json()

        if "categoriesAnalysis" in result:
            for category_analysis in result["categoriesAnalysis"]:
                category = category_analysis["category"]
                severity = category_analysis["severity"]

                if category in thresholds:
                    if severity > thresholds[category]:
                        return False  # Content exceeds the threshold for this category
            return True  # All categories are within thresholds or not specified
        else:
            # If no categoriesAnalysis, assume allowed (or log a warning if unexpected)
            return True
    except requests.exceptions.RequestException as e:
        print(f"Error calling Azure Content Safety API: {e}")
        # Depending on the application's requirements, you might want to
        # re-raise the exception, return False (fail-safe), or return True (fail-open).
        # For this example, we'll assume a problem with the service means we can't verify safety,
        # so we might return False to be cautious.
        return False
